seo.title: Masseria Le Carrube: Adults-Only Puglia Honeymoon (2026)
seo.description: Adults-only boutique masseria near Ostuni. Score 81/100, from $500/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: Masseria Le Carrube is the adults-only intimate alternative to the great Puglian luxury masserias — a small (32-room) 18th-century farmhouse on a 12-acre carob and olive estate on the road between Ostuni and the Adriatic, owned by the Melograni family and run as a quiet, design-conscious, no-children boutique. It is, by some distance, the most peaceful honeymoon address in the Itria Valley. The aesthetic is restrained Pugliese — white-washed stone walls, gnarled old olive beams, hand-thrown ceramic basins, linen sheets, and the original carob (carrubo) trees still standing in the gardens. The single saltwater pool sits in an old olive grove with the white town of Ostuni visible on the hill 4km away. The Trattoria Mangiamus (the on-site restaurant) is excellent at a modest level — burrata flown daily from Andria, orecchiette made by hand each morning, grilled total fish from the Adriatic 8km away, a small but precisely chosen Pugliese wine list. The spa is small (four treatment rooms, hammam, no thermal pools) but the treatments use locally-grown almond oil and the operation is unhurried. No beach club — the closest beach is a 15-minute drive — and no golf, no kids’ club, no buzz, no events. The honeymoon move is one of the Junior Suites in the original masseria farmhouse with a private terrace overlooking the olive groves, or one of the new Garden Suites at the back with a private outdoor shower. The defining moment: 9am breakfast in the carob garden, your own table under a 200-year-old carob tree, with fresh ricotta, marmalade made from the property’s own bergamot, and Pugliese honey from the on-site hives. Caveats: this is not a full-luxury experience — no Michelin restaurant, no thalasso, no big spa, no beach on-site; service is warm but not choreographed at the Borgo Egnazia or Aman level; and the immediate setting is rural Puglian rather than dramatic. But for honeymooners who specifically want adults-only quiet, real Pugliese intimacy, and a property they will mostly have to themselves outside August, Le Carrube is the clear choice.
content.best_room: A Junior Suite in the original masseria with private terrace overlooking the olive groves. The new Garden Suites at the back with private outdoor shower are the alternative. Avoid the standard rooms in the converted stables — lovely but smaller and without the private outdoor space.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival and Mangiamus dinner
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 30 minutes from Brindisi. Check-in to your Junior Suite, welcome Spumante. Aperitivo in the carob garden. Dinner at Trattoria Mangiamus on the terrace.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Ostuni white town
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 10 minutes to Ostuni (la città bianca). Morning wandering the white-washed lanes. Lunch at Osteria del Tempo Perso. Afternoon back at the pool. Dinner at the masseria.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Beach day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 15 minutes to Costa Merlata or Torre Pozzelle for the Adriatic. Long beach morning. Lunch at a beach trattoria. Spa afternoon back at the masseria.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Itria white towns
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver-and-guide to Locorotondo, Cisternino, Alberobello. Lunch at a Cisternino fornello. Return for the pool and dinner at the masseria.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow garden day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Late breakfast under the carob tree. Yoga in the garden. Cooking class for orecchiette. Lunch with your pasta. Afternoon massage. Quiet dinner.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Lecce day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver to Lecce (1h). Private baroque tour. Lunch at Bros’ (1 Michelin star). Return for final dinner at the masseria.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast under the carob tree. Drive to Brindisi for departure.

caveats: No on-site beach club, no Michelin restaurant, no thalasso. This is intimate, not full-luxury.
Spa is small (4 rooms, no thermal pools). Use the day spa at Borgo Egnazia (15 min) if needed.
Service is warm but not choreographed at the Borgo Egnazia or Aman level.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Among the most peaceful adults-only honeymoons in Italy. The 32-room scale, carob gardens, and no-children policy create a unique atmosphere.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May, June, September, and early October. Closed late November to mid-March.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Junior Suites 4–6 months for May–September. August requires 9 months.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: Yes — strict adults-only policy (16+). The atmosphere is genuinely peaceful.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Junior Suite in the original masseria with private terrace. Garden Suite for the contemporary option.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Brindisi (BDS) 30 minutes. Bari (BRI) 75 minutes. Hire car at airport — the masseria is rural and needs one.
